input.rationale: The fixed experiment 708eebc14c4040feb495e11d064001d0-experiment has now been executed by the controller, so this update turns the source-grounded behaviours into an execution-grounded conclusion and records one observed instance as durable knowledge. It also opens a second sourced question in the same area, on whether a peer-supplied MsgReadIndex with an empty Entries slice reaches the leader's read-index producer, because the captured dispatch code treats MsgReadIndex as a term-less local message and validates the entry count only for MsgReadIndexResp.

knowledge.assertion: The second admission with an equal rctx is discarded, so the leader keeps exactly one pending status and one stored request message for the two admissions.
Completion answers only the stored first request message, so a discarded equal-rctx admission produces neither a MsgReadIndexResp nor a ReadState.

investigations.question: Can a MsgReadIndex with an empty Entries slice reach the leader's read-index producer and panic the node, or is the message rejected, dropped or validated before the producer dereferences Entries[0]?
investigations.hypothesis: MsgReadIndex is sent and forwarded without a term (raft.go:536-541 keeps the local-message treatment for MsgProp/MsgReadIndex), a follower forwards it unchanged to its leader while a leader passes it straight to sendMsgReadIndexResponse (raft.go:1759-1765, 1346-1363), and that producer dereferences m.Entries[0] in readOnly.addRequest and responseToReadIndexReq without checking the slice length; only MsgReadIndexResp has an entry-count check (raft.go:1766-1772) and only MsgProp has an explicit empty-entry panic (raft.go:1286-1289). The apparent mismatch is therefore that the same message shape is validated for the response direction and for proposals but not for the request direction entering the leader's producer.
investigations.discriminator: Step a MsgReadIndex carrying no Entries into a follower (expected: forwarded to its leader, raft.go:1759-1765) and into a leader (expected by this hypothesis: an index-out-of-range panic inside the read-index producer), then step a well-formed one-entry MsgReadIndex into the same node as a positive control. Use a recovering wrapper that records the recovered value plus the leader's state, term and readOnly queue/pending sizes at the moment of the panic, and compare with the empty-MsgProp path that panics deliberately. If the empty-Entries message is instead dropped, converted to an error or silently ignored, the hypothesis is refuted and the observed disposition is the finding.
limitations: A malformed or forged peer message may be considered outside the trusted transport contract, so a panic here would be an availability/robustness question rather than a divergence from consensus; the question is registered to establish the actual behaviour first.
The discriminator has not been executed yet; the hypothesis is provisional and rests only on the captured dispatch and producer code.
The node-to-transport boundary is not part of the captured package, so reachability through a real peer depends on what the embedding application forwards to Node.Step.

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the fixed experiment (three-voter cluster {1,2,3} in one process, node 1 leader in term 1 with a committed entry in its term, ReadOnlySafe, fault-free ordered delivery), the ReadIndex request admitted first (parsed event 1, requester 2, rctx 'assurance-dup-rctx') received one MsgReadIndexResp and one ReadState, while the equal-rctx request admitted second (event 2, requester 3) received no MsgReadIndexResp and no ReadState (event 13: responded=false, responses=0, requester_read_states=0) over the following eight leader heartbeat rounds (events 4-11: leader_state=StateLeader, pending=0, undelivered=0, cumulative responses_to_3=0) whose acknowledgments were produced by the real follower state machines. With two different rctxes both requesters were answered (events 15-18), and with a single requester retrying its own rctx that requester was answered (events 20-21).
knowledge.conditions: One executed in-process experiment with the fixed harness bytes of experiment 708eebc14c4040feb495e11d064001d0-experiment (receipt 5827db69173840a595c972e79565bcde, exit 0, changed_target_files []); no packet loss, no election after node 1 became leader, no membership change, no snapshot; the second admission arrived while the first status was still pending. This is one observed instance, not a universal guarantee.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 5827db69173840a595c972e79565bcde is a completed execution of this investigation's own experiment (status completed, exit 0, outcome tests_passed, changed_target_files [], no parsing errors, 22 parsed events). Comparison 0 asks whether every admitted ReadIndex request that carries an rctx equal to another requester's pending rctx receives a read index answer; it is violated with a complete valid witness at parsed index 13. Event 13 is the delivery observation for request_id 'duplicate/3' with responded=false, responses=0, requester_read_states=0 and rounds_waited=8, and the prerequisite correlation links it to its own admission at index 2 (read_index_request for requester 3, rctx 'assurance-dup-rctx'), whose measured operands are pending_after=1 and queue_after=1: the admission produced no new pending status compared with requester 2's admission at index 1. Index 12 is the matched positive counterpart for request_id 'duplicate/2' (responded=true, responses=1), so the two admissions differ only in requester identity. Index 3 records a third, identical retry from requester 3: it was stepped into the leader (two heartbeats emitted, leader_state=StateLeader) while queue_before=1 and queue_after=1, so the retry was processed and discarded in the same way and no error was returned on the caller path (rawnode.go:560-563 discards the Step error). Events 4-11 are the observation window: the leader stayed in StateLeader with pending=0, queue=0, undelivered=0 and cumulative responses_to_3=0 across eight rounds in which the heartbeat acknowledgments were produced by the real follower state machines, so repeated nonprogress is not attributable to a stalled leader, an unprocessed message queue or a lost quorum. The mechanism is the sourced one: readOnly.addRequest discards a second admission with an equal rctx without storing its request message (read_only.go:56-63), and completion answers only rs.req through responseToReadIndexReq (raft.go:1596-1606, 2068-2084), so the discarded admission can never receive either a local ReadState or a MsgReadIndexResp. The two controls exclude alternative explanations with the same sampling and the same delivery mechanics: comparison 1 (identical shape, distinct rctxes) holds at indices 17 and 18, and comparison 2 (a single requester retrying its own rctx) holds at index 21, so the read path itself, the harness and the leader's progress are functional. This is a bounded liveness result for the documented caller contract: node.go:218-229 tells callers that a lost ReadIndex request is theirs to retry and asserts that reusing an rctx is supported from release-3.7 on, while the observed behaviour silently discards such a retry instead of answering it.

knowledge.assertion: The equal-rctx admission is discarded at admission time (pending_after/queue_after unchanged at parsed indices 1 and 2).
Completion answers only the first admission's request message, which is why index 13 shows no response for requester 3 while index 12 shows the response for requester 2.

counterevidence: node.go:218-229 documents that callers must not reuse an rctx in release-3.6 and only states that the restriction is lifted starting with release-3.7, so the silent drop can be read as the documented restriction of this revision rather than an implementation error; the execution establishes the mechanism and the starvation, and the classification is left to human review.

The same-requester retry is answered (index 21), so the finding does not generalise to every retry: starvation was only observed when a different requester's equal-rctx admission was discarded because another requester had been admitted first.

The distinct-rctx control holds (indices 17 and 18), which shows the read path and the harness deliver answers when admissions are not coalesced; the violation therefore depends on rctx equality rather than on a generally broken experiment.
Only one execution in one process is cited; the eight-round window and the fault-free delivery assumption bound what the observation supports.
limitations: ReadOnlyLeaseBased, the pendingReadIndexMessages path for a leader without a committed entry in its term, membership change, snapshots, restarts and leadership change were not exercised.

The requester-side application contract (matching ReadStates by RequestCtx) is taken from node.go / rawnode.go rather than executed, so the observation is about the producer's answers, not about an application-level read result.
The retained execution establishes repeated nonprogress under normal quorum acknowledgments in one run; it is not an unbounded guarantee and does not exclude a future or external repair.
Whether a coalesced duplicate rctx can additionally mis-attribute a stale read index to a later distinct read request was not investigated.
interpretations.report_title: ReadIndex 复用同一 rctx 时的静默丢弃：第二个请求方在 leader 正常运行时收不到读索引应答
interpretations.report_answer: 在快照 release-3.6 代码上，leader 处于 StateLeader 且使用 ReadOnlySafe 时，待处理读请求只以 rctx 字符串为键：requester 2 的请求先被接受后，requester 3 携带相同 rctx 的请求被 addRequest 直接丢弃（admission 后 pending/queue 仍为 1），随后由真实 follower 产生的 quorum 心跳确认只完成 2 的那条状态，3 在 8 轮心跳中既没有 MsgReadIndexResp 也没有 ReadState（responded=false），而 leader 始终为 StateLeader、无未投递消息。对照场景（rctx 不同，或同一请求方自重试）都能得到应答。源码注释同时要求调用方自行重试并宣称 3.7 起允许复用 rctx，因此该静默丢弃是否构成缺陷由人工复核判定。

investigations.question: On a stable leader using ReadOnlySafe, can a ReadIndex request that carries an rctx equal to one that is still pending complete, or is that request silently discarded so that its requester receives no read index answer while the cluster keeps making progress?
investigations.hypothesis: The leader keys pending read requests by the rctx string only, so a second admission carrying an equal rctx is dropped without recording its own request message; when the single status completes, the answer is addressed to the first admission's requester and no answer is ever produced for the second requester, even though the leader stays leader and keeps satisfying quorum heartbeat acknowledgments.
investigations.discriminator: Drive two real voters to forward ReadIndex messages with equal rctx to the leader before any quorum acknowledgment, then deliver the quorum ack and eight further heartbeat rounds with acks from both followers; count read index answers per requester while confirming the leader stays in StateLeader. Controls: the identical shape with distinct rctxes (both requesters must be answered) and a single requester retrying its own rctx (that requester must be answered), which separate a duplicate-rctx admission loss from a broken harness or a generally stalled leader.
counterevidence: node.go:218-229 states that callers must not reuse an rctx and that the reuse restriction is only lifted starting with release-3.7, so the silent drop may be the documented behaviour of this release-3.6 revision rather than an implementation error; this draft reports the mechanism and the observed starvation, and leaves that classification to human review.

The same-requester retry case is answered: when one requester retries its own rctx while the status is pending, the single response is addressed to that requester, so the observed starvation requires a requester whose equal-rctx message is discarded because another requester was admitted first.

Existing test coverage (raft_test.go:1192-1222) exercises one unique rctx and only checks that the queue and pending map drain; node_test.go:196-241 forwards two equal rctxes from different nodes but asserts only that the messages are forwarded and never checks for read index answers.
limitations: Only ReadOnlySafe is exercised; ReadOnlyLeaseBased and the pendingReadIndexMessages path (a leader that has not yet committed an entry in its term) are out of scope for this experiment.
The observation window is eight leader heartbeat rounds with quorum acknowledgments in one process; it establishes repeated nonprogress under normal opportunities rather than an unbounded guarantee.
The requester-side application contract (matching ReadStates by RequestCtx) is read from node.go / rawnode.go rather than executed.

knowledge.statement: In StateLeader with the ReadOnlySafe option, when a MsgReadIndex arrives whose Entries[0].Data equals the rctx of a request that is already recorded in readOnly.pendingReadIndex, readOnly.addRequest returns early without storing the new request message, and sendMsgReadIndexResponse still attaches a heartbeat with that rctx (bcastHeartbeatWithCtx) and re-acknowledges the local node; the readIndexQueue and pendingReadIndex therefore keep exactly one status for the two admissions, and no second request message is retained.
knowledge.conditions: Node is in StateLeader, ReadOnlyOption is ReadOnlySafe (the default), the leader has committed an entry in its current term so stepLeader calls sendMsgReadIndexResponse directly, the earlier request with the equal rctx is still pending (not yet advanced), and no reset/become* has occurred between the two admissions.

knowledge.statement: On the acknowledging heartbeat, stepLeader asks readOnly.advance for the statuses up to the acknowledged ctx and then answers each returned status through responseToReadIndexReq(rs.req, rs.index): a status whose stored request came from a remote peer produces one MsgReadIndexResp addressed to that stored request's From, and a status whose stored request came from the leader itself appends one local ReadState. Only the request message of the first admission with a given rctx is stored, so admissions that were discarded by addRequest produce no read index answer of either kind.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe with a quorum of heartbeat acknowledgments carrying the ctx, leader state unchanged between admission and acknowledgment, and the discarded admission having used the same rctx bytes as the stored one.
